question.worked_solution:
We're given that $Z∼N(0,1),$ and we wish to compute $P(Z\ge -1.42).$ The required probability is represented by the area shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14254773/assets/c65e0b1c20626e259a638cf9b0ba2690294eb1b0a63759728ac0c35143478f5f.png)

By the definition of the cumulative distribution function $Φ(z),$ 

$$
P(Z\le z)=Φ(z).
$$

Since the total area under the graph equals $1,$ we can express the required probability in terms of $Φ(z)$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(Z\ge -1.42) & =1-P(Z<-1.42) \\  & =1-Φ(-1.42)\end{aligned}
$$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14254773/assets/6cb07863868a37238c8856c2dc28d96b023558fa7d10df7a5c6332735ec53146.png)

From the table, we know that

$$
Φ(-1.42)=0.0778.
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P(Z\ge -1.42) & =1-Φ(-1.42) \\  & =1-0.0778 \\  & =0.9222.\end{aligned}
$$
